correctness.rationale: The product character is a homomorphism because the top is abelian and translations permute the factors; every base tuple determines exactly one top coordinate in the kernel. The balanced base projects onto each factor by using a second coordinate to cancel the character, and every top element has a lift. A central element moving the coordinates cannot fix a singleton supported in ker chi; if chi is injective and |T|>2, it cannot fix an opposite pair supported at x,y with the moved x outside {x,y}. Coordinate surjectivity then forces a central base tuple to have entries in Z(R), and top surjectivity forces them to agree. Conversely, each such diagonal is in the kernel since chi(c)^|T|=1 and it commutes with the full wreath product. In the remaining case an element with base (a,1) and top a squares to the nonidentity diagonal, hence generates the order-four kernel. Since the group order changes by |R| to |R|^|T| at each step, an exceptional step can occur only initially. The A4×C5 seeds and p=3,5 towers are as in Damele and give center C5 and order 60^(p^m). The argument is uniform, not an extrapolation from nine finite examples; the uploaded checker was inspected, not run.

evidence: Damele constructs the kernel and proves the availability of diagonal and balanced elements and top lifts. Skuratovskii–Williams give center conditions for a full permutational wreath product, not this subgroup.

residual_risks: The bounded comparisons do not rule out an equivalent theorem about centers of balanced subgroups under different terminology. Ordinary wreath-product results alone do not settle that question.

value.rationale: An exact multiplicative-group center is useful for distinguishing the invariants of growing simple skew braces from their additive-group structure. The classification settles all allowed quotient choices at once, including uniqueness of the only possible enlargement, and reads off a persistent C5 in both natural A5 towers without enumerating their elements. The prior C4 computation alone is not the contribution.
